# Scrib SU -- 2026-08-24

First standup of the eight-week build, about 46 minutes. Pankaj joined partway
through, around the 40-minute mark, after a conflicting call. Rob: "we went a
little over and that's fine."

## Summary

- Rob walked the team through the new Teams channel, the Lucid open-questions
  board, the backlog HTML with spikes, and the meta repo (this wiki/brain
  repo), explaining how it feeds the JIRA work and captures learnings for
  reuse on future projects.
- The team agreed to call the eight-week build the MVP, not the POC, to avoid
  confusing it with Rob's earlier prototype.
- iOS staffing is thin this week: Neelesh is out on emergency leave, and a
  second iOS engineer is onboarding 2026-08-25 or 2026-08-26, modeled at full
  time alongside Neelesh at roughly 0.6, mirroring the backend split with
  Pankaj and Nitish.
- Rob demoed the current POC/prototype. It runs on Expo Go with a real AWS
  backend built in Terraform (borrowed from a colleague's agent, reviewed by
  an AWS expert), costing about $25-28/month so far. The app dropped its
  speech-to-text translation step; a day entry is now either typed text or a
  played-back voice recording, with almost no AI left in the app itself.
- No confirmed Apple developer account yet. Pramod flagged that if Bounteous
  has no umbrella account and a new one has to be created, Apple's process
  could eat a meaningful slice of the two-month cycle. Expo Go is the interim
  QA path; the team believes it covers enough native surface (Skia rendering
  worked in the POC) for a fair amount of testing, though this is unconfirmed.
  Rob asks the client about an Apple developer account at the 2026-08-25
  workshop.
- QA (Karuna) raised how builds get handed to QA. For now QA runs the app
  locally (build and run locally, or emulator); on-device install follows once
  accounts and test devices are in place. Pramod is checking with Bounteous IT
  on devices.
- Karuna raised test case documentation. Jira's native test handling felt too
  heavy for the team's flow. The group agreed to start in Excel, sharable with
  the whole team, with Karuna setting the QA standard. Pramod will check
  whether Bounteous has a licensed test management tool (X-ray-class or
  TestRail-class) as a longer-term option, and separately whether the client's
  existing system already uses any test management software.
- Nitish asked about target audience: the eight-week build targets AWS
  re:Invent at year end, where the client wants to demo via QR code download.
  Initial testing is small (the team plus some of the client's team), scaling
  to roughly 800 testers later as more funding lands. The client's stated
  competition/positioning is apps like Wordle and Strava.
- Pankaj (once he joined) shared a revised assumptions questionnaire, having
  resolved most open questions on his own, with two known exceptions: under-13
  handling and COPPA, which need a signed agreement and are hard to do in
  phase one, and self-signup vs. invite-only onboarding. Onboarding will be
  invite-only at the start, seeded with a few default users who invite others.
  Rob asked Pankaj to build his architecture/assumptions writeup as a wiki
  page in this repo rather than a standalone doc.
- Nitish asked whether Lucid board questions should go to the team first or
  straight to the client; Rob said either path is fine, run it through the
  Teams channel first if the team wants visibility before the client sees it.
- Pramod could not open share controls on the Lucid board at the start of the
  call; Rob granted him edit/share live and re-sent Nitish an invitation, but
  neither confirmed the grant landed by the end of the call.

## Questions / decisions

### Decisions

- Call the eight-week build the MVP, not the POC, so it is not confused with Rob's earlier prototype. Owner: Pramod Kumar.
- Model iOS staffing as one full-time engineer plus Neelesh at roughly 0.6, matching the backend shape. Owner: Pramod Kumar.
- Keep PTO in the existing Excel tracker and team access in the existing tracker, both linked from the Scribl Dev Team channel; no new board or calendar. Owner: Rob Forshier II.
- The Lucid board is the one place for running client-facing open questions; anyone can add a question there directly, or run it through the Teams channel first if they want team visibility before the client sees it. Owner: Rob Forshier II.
- Start test case documentation in Excel rather than Jira's native handling, which felt too heavy for the team's flow. Karuna sets the QA standard. Owners: Karuna Arshakota, Rob Forshier II.
- QA starts on a local build (run locally or on an emulator), with on-device install to follow once accounts and test devices are available. Owners: Rob Forshier II, Pramod Kumar.
- Onboarding is invite-only at the start, seeded with a few default users who invite others. Owner: Rob Forshier II made the invite-only call; Pankaj Aggarwal proposed the default-user seeding mechanism.
- The meta repo's index.html and README are the onboarding path into the wiki/brain repo, rather than a separate Confluence-style space. Owner: Rob Forshier II. Rob was describing practice already in place, not making a fresh call in this meeting.

### Questions

- Does the client have an Apple developer account, and can Bounteous stand one up and transfer it later? On the board for the 2026-08-25 workshop.
- Does the client's existing system use any test management software the handover could land on?
- Does Bounteous have a licensed test management tool (X-ray-class or TestRail-class) the team could use instead of Excel? Pramod checking internally.
- How much of Expo Go's native module surface covers the app? Skia rendering worked in the prototype, so the team expects enough coverage for real QA, but this is unconfirmed.
- Under-13 and COPPA handling: Pankaj flags it needs a signed agreement, making it hard in phase one. Rob's read is it stays out of the eight weeks but is kept in mind. Not yet resolved either way.
- Self-signup beyond the invite-only start is not scoped, and Pankaj asked whether it is even planned; not answered on the call beyond "invite only at the beginning."
